predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws these lands inside the Holy Roman Empire shape and, from 1260, inside Holy Roman Empire Minor States.

successors.note: Cliopatria has Electorate of Baden 1803..1805 and Grand Duchy of Baden from 1806 (eu-20). The 1803 additions are theirs.

capitals.name: Baden-Baden (Hohenbaden)
capitals.note: The seat of the 12th century (infobox); 'In 1219 he moved his seat of power to Pforzheim'.

capitals.name: Pforzheim
capitals.note: Seat from 1219. After the 1535 division it remained the Baden-Durlach capital to 1565 (Baden-Durlach infobox 'Pforzheim (1535-1565)'); the Baden-Baden line resided at Baden-Baden (New Castle from 1479) until 1705 and at Rastatt after.

capitals.name: Durlach
capitals.note: 'The residence moved from Pforzheim to Karlsburg Castle in Durlach in 1565' (Baden-Durlach infobox Durlach 1565-1718).

capitals.name: Karlsruhe
capitals.note: Infobox 'Karlsruhe 1715-1803'; Karlsruhe Palace begun 1715 (the Baden-Durlach page gives 1718 for the capital).

correction.text: the margraviate round Hohenbaden: Baden-Baden, Rastatt and Ettlingen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Baden row). The page: Hohenbaden Castle begun about 1100, 'when completed in 1112, he marked the occasion by adopting the title of a Margrave of Baden'. It gives no boundary or area before 1771 (infobox '1,350 sq mi (3,500 km2)'); the Baden-Baden page's 'core territory extended from Ettlingen to Steinbach' is read as an 18 km circle at Rastatt (about 1,000 km2), soft.

correction.text: with Pforzheim (seat from 1219) and the Hachberg and Markgräflerland lands of the cadet lines

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Baden-Hochberg ... Founded in 1190, it lasted until 1418, when it too died with no male heirs' (Hachberg is centred on Emmendingen, the Markgräflerland ran between Müllheim and Lörrach with Sausenberg, Rötteln and Badenweiler: Baden-Durlach page). Pforzheim, Durlach, Emmendingen and Müllheim-Lörrach are drawn as circles of 13, 10, 10 and 15 km. The cadet lines are kept inside the state: they are the same dynasty and the page treats them as parts of the margraviate.

correction.text: with half of Lahr and Mahlberg (1442)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The consolidation of the margraviate came in 1442.' Half of the Lahr and Mahlberg dominions joined Baden. A 10 km circle at Lahr-Mahlberg; the total drawn is about 3,300 km2 against the infobox 3,500 km2 (the 1771 combined margraviate). The Baden-Durlach infobox gives 1,631 km2 for that half alone. The 1535-1771 division into Baden-Baden and Baden-Durlach, the 1594-1622 Durlach occupation of Baden-Baden and the 1629 Lahr-Mahlberg partition are internal and do not change the outline.

ledger.note: 1112: 'it was named a margraviate in 1112.' Hohenbaden Castle was begun about 1100; 'when completed in 1112, he marked the occasion by adopting the title of a Margrave of Baden.'

region.text: the lands round Hohenbaden Castle and Baden-Baden

ledger.note: 1190: the Hachberg line is founded (page silent on how the lands came to the house). 'Baden-Hochberg ... Founded in 1190, it lasted until 1418, when it too died with no male heirs.' The page does not say how the Hachberg and Sausenberg lands (Emmendingen, Markgräflerland) came to the house, so this is a bridge: a cadet line inside the state, dated at the line's foundation.

region.text: the Hachberg lands round Emmendingen and the Markgräflerland, with Pforzheim

ledger.note: 1219: 'In 1219 he moved his seat of power to Pforzheim.'

1442: Lahr and Mahlberg. 'The consolidation of the margraviate came in 1442.' Half of the Lahr and Mahlberg dominions joined Baden; the page names no seller. The other half was held with Nassau-Saarbrücken to 1629 (Baden-Baden page).

region.text: half of the Lahr and Mahlberg dominions

ledger.note: 1565: 'The residence moved from Pforzheim to Karlsburg Castle in Durlach in 1565' (Baden-Durlach line; the Baden-Baden line resided at Baden-Baden until 1705, then Rastatt).
1715: Karlsruhe. Charles III William began Karlsruhe Palace 'from 1715', the start of the city of Karlsruhe (infobox 'Karlsruhe 1715-1803').

21 October 1771: the two lines reunite. 'After Augustus George's death on 21 October 1771' Charles Frederick of Baden-Durlach inherited Baden-Baden; 'For the third and last time, all the Badener lands became united under a single ruler.' Inside this one state, so the outline does not change.

1803: 'The restored Margraviate of Baden was elevated to the status of electorate in 1803.' Charles Frederick gained the Prince-Bishopric of Constance (the part east of the Rhine), parts of the Rhenish Palatinate and several smaller districts; in 1806 the Electorate became the Grand Duchy of Baden.

wars.name: Mainz Archbishops' Feud (Baden's part)
wars.outcome: 'He had to surrender several of his territories to the Electoral Palatinate and its allies' (Margrave Charles I, defeated in 1462).
wars.note: The page names neither the lands nor the year of the surrender, so no loss event is entered. The page gives only 1462 for the dispute.

wars.name: Occupation of Baden-Baden by Baden-Durlach

zones.text: the Baden-Baden half of the margraviate

wars.outcome: 'Baden-Durlach occupied Baden-Baden from 1594 to 1622'; it ended after the defeat at Wimpfen on 6 May 1622.
wars.note: Internal to the state, hence no occupation event.

wars.name: Nine Years' War devastation of Baden
wars.outcome: 'In 1689, Mélac systematically burnt all the cities and villages of Baden, except for Gernsbach'; Pforzheim and Durlach were burned.
wars.note: No land changed hands on the pages opened.

certainty.note: The pages give castles, towns and cadet lines, not boundaries; the only dated acquisition is half of Lahr-Mahlberg in 1442 and the Peace of Westphalia restored the 1550 situation.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Baden row before the Electorate of Baden (1803-1805).

SCOPE. One state for the Margraviate of Baden with its cadet lines (Hachberg, Sausenberg, Pforzheim; Baden-Baden and Baden-Durlach 1535-1771), as the Baden page treats it; the divisions are internal and not ledger events. Ends 1803 when the electorate (Cliopatria's Electorate of Baden, eu-20) begins; its additions of 1803 (Constance, Palatine districts) are theirs.

SHAPES are circles (gazetteer lacks the towns): Rastatt 8.20E 48.86N 18 km; Pforzheim 8.70E 48.89N 13 km; Durlach 8.40E 48.99N 10 km; Emmendingen 7.85E 48.12N 10 km; Müllheim-Lörrach 7.65E 47.75N 15 km; Lahr-Mahlberg 7.84E 48.31N 10 km. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Baden-Baden', 'Rastatt', 'Pforzheim', 'Durlach', 'Emmendingen', 'Lörrach', 'Lahr', 'Offenburg' (the gazetteer has Karlsruhe only).

NOT SETTLED. (1) The Hachberg and Sausenberg lands: the page gives the lines' dates (Hachberg 1190-1418; Sausenberg reverting to Baden-Baden in 1503; the Pforzheim line 1291-1361 as a note) but not their territory or heirs, so the 1190 gain is a bridge at confidence 2 with counterpart 'nobody'. (2) The 1462 surrender to the Palatinate and its allies: no lands, no year of surrender on the page. (3) The left-bank cession to France: the Baden page's year for it is 1792 (the usual Treaty of Basel / Paris dates are later), no lands named; not entered. (4) The Ortenau: Baden-Baden received the rights to the Landvogtei of Offenburg in 1701 and it reverted to the Emperor under the 1765 treaty (Baden-Baden page); not entered (rights, not territory). (5) The Eberstein county was de facto Baden-Baden until 1660 (Gernsbach); not entered. (6) The Baden-Baden and Baden-Durlach shapes are not separated. (7) The Peace of Westphalia restored the 1550 situation; no map change recorded.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: lordship-of-lahr-mahlberg (to 1442 and 1629), county-of-eberstein, margraviate-of-baden-hachberg (1190-1418) if the cadet lines are wanted as states, electorate-of-baden (eu-20).
